newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ampol sees fewer Australian petroleum refineries.
newsitem.headline: Ampol sees fewer Australian petroleum refineries.

text.p: Australia's largest petrol retailer, Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (Ampol) said Australia's petroleum refining and retailing industry was suffering from low financial returns and over-regulation, which he predicted will lead to closure of some refineries.
"Oil companies are being strangled by regulation," Ian Blackburne, managing director of Ampol told a conference of Australian oil and gas producers on Wednesday.
"If current trends continue, there will be fewer refineries and other facilities will be rationalised," he said.
Blackburne criticised federal regulations which he said were distorted to give importers and independent petroleum suppliers an unfair market advantage.
"Some regulators and policymakers seem wedded to the notion that major brands don't compete and regard every commercial move as a conspiracy against the public interest," Blackburne said.
Ampol is equally owned by Caltex Australia Ltd and Pioneer International Ltd, which has said it is considering selling the Ampol stake.
